reelection.rule: Rule: end of the current class term in legislators-current.yaml. Class 2 ends 2027-01-03. The November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file does not store the election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 Senate votes, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 22. Nay or No: 7. Not Voting: 11. Of 29 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 27 (93%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 51 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: Senate votes 1–262 of the 119th Congress, session 2 (262 votes, January 5, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the Senate LIS.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text: On Veterans Day, we honor the brave men and women who have answered the call to serve our nation. Their courage, sacrifice, and unwavering commitment to defending our freedoms represent the very best of America. North Carolina is proudly home to over 600,000 veterans, and we are forever grateful for their service to our state and nation.

.@PeteHegseth, cabinet secretaries shouldn't be wasting taxpayer dollars on campaign style videos. Kristi Noem learned that the hard way. 

This is about you: the incompetence you’ve displayed, the bad advice you’ve given to president, and your shameful and embarassing episodes https://t.co/ZBeY4qjyNc

Congratulations to our next Senator @RoyCooperNC. I look forward to working with him during the transition. Representing the Old North State in the world’s most deliberative body is an honor of a lifetime and Susan and I wish Roy and Kristin the very best in the years ahead.
Susan and I are praying for Senator Murphy and wishing him a full and speedy recovery. We’re encouraged to hear he is responding to treatment and are keeping Chris and his family in our thoughts.

Happy 251st Birthday to the @USMC! North Carolina is proud to be home to Camp Lejeune, MCAS Cherry Point, and MCAS New River. To our active-duty Marines, veterans, and military families: thank you for your unwavering dedication and sacrifice in defense of our nation. #SemperFi https://t.co/mqGbBnYpWI

The shifting explanations from Musk and the administration sound like Abbott and Costello’s “Who’s on First?” Except the consequences for Ukrainian civilians are deadly.

Musk says he didn’t do it. The administration says it didn’t either. Yet someone in the administration

If these reports are true, this is a welcome development. It’s now been over a week since Starshield service in Ukraine was throttled, and innocent Ukrainians have bore the murderous brunt. We’ve spent that week trying to determine the party responsible, but they have yet to own https://t.co/bGNGOLyngV

WTF, Steve? Look up the definition of “humanitarian.” What an embarrassing and outrageous thing to say. You should go back to Ukraine and ask the families of the children Putin has kidnapped and murdered whether they agree your friend Putin is a “humanitarian.” https://t.co/Nbu0wKPmby https://t.co/SMQiTy46cc

Beyond irresponsible. What part of enforcing a law passed 86-11 by the Senate does the President and his advisors not understand? It’s unconscionable that this administration is capitulating to a Russian dictator who illegally invaded Ukraine and butchers innocent civilians every single day. If the President wants to actually bring down energy prices, he can do it by solving the Iran problem, not by doing a solid for Vladimir Putin.

https://t.co/ccCakQUTDt

The latest reporting suggests this strategic snafu may have occurred more locally within DOD Starshield systems, not with Starlink or SpaceX. 

I’m not holding my breath for Defense Secretary Hegseth to offer transparency, so we’ll be asking the DOD Inspector General to initiate an investigation and report back to Congress and the American People. 

Meanwhile, both Ukrainian civilians and U.S. diplomatic and security personnel were placed at unnecessary risk and without warning. 

At best, this was an unacceptable error or lapse, and at worst a conscience decision to clear the field for a Russian attack.

.@elonmusk please tell me these overnight disruptions to Starlink terminals in Ukraine were unintended - that @SpaceX is doing everything it can to fix a temporary glitch.

I'm confident this does not reflect a change in SpaceX policy because if so, intentionally degrading Ukraine's ability to defend itself might be construed as aiding and abetting a mass murderer. Can you confirm that's not SpaceX’s intent?

Ukrainians simply want to live in peace. They did not ask Putin to bomb their homes, schools and hospitals. They do not want Putin to kidnap and brainwash their children. They are not interested in destroying energy infrastructure - in Ukraine or in Russia. They only want to defend their country and live their lives.

Supporting Ukrainian sovereignty - or at the very least, allowing for it - should not be a gray area for the U.S. government or for American corporations. Can you clarify the SpaceX position?  

https://t.co/cPtszYRzSz

We should be holding Putin accountable for his aggression, not helping fund his war against Ukraine. That’s why I joined my colleagues in calling on the administration to reverse course on Russian diesel imports and uphold the sanctions Congress put in place.

https://t.co/IaBEhuiPpD

Following recent heavy rainfall across North Carolina, my team and I are closely monitoring rising water levels and local flood warnings in the mountains. With our communities still rebuilding after the catastrophic impacts of Helene, we know how vulnerable these areas remain. Please follow instructions from local emergency management, avoid flooded roadways, and stay safe.

Hasan should face the death penalty, but making his execution public and streaming it? Beyond disgusting. Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America. https://t.co/qpl6KQj4Wb

Today, we remember the innocent lives lost in Hamas’ horrific attack on Israel three years ago. We must never forget the evil we witnessed on Oct. 7 or the pain so many families continue to bear. I remain committed to standing with our friend and ally Israel and supporting its right to defend itself.

Great news for Western North Carolina! As an original cosponsor of the Great American Outdoors Act, I’m proud to have helped secure the funding for this $100 million investment to restore 75 miles of the Blue Ridge Parkway, supporting visitors and local communities. 

https://t.co/jwdR88CyqU

Congratulations to Brian S. Meyers and Philip L. Aubart on their nominations to serve as District Court Judges for North Carolina’s Eastern and Middle Districts. Both are highly qualified attorneys who respect the rule of law and are committed to upholding the Constitution. I am confident they will serve the people of North Carolina with integrity and distinction. I thank President Trump for nominating them and look forward to working with @SenTedBuddNC to advance their nominations and secure their confirmation by the full Senate.

I commend the Office of Inspector General for its comprehensive analysis of the Fed’s renovation costs. While the report makes clear there was no fraud or criminal wrongdoing by the Fed or any member of the Board, it also makes clear there should have been better procedures and project management expertise for a project of this scale. The entire federal government, from the executive branch to entities with statutory independence like the Fed, has an obligation to be transparent and good stewards of taxpayer dollars. I appreciate Chair Warsh’s commitment to both protecting Fed independence and inviting Congressional oversight.
Thank you to @NCDOT and all the crews working around the clock to reopen roads and keep North Carolinians moving safely. https://t.co/d27o1pGzDC

On the second anniversary of Helene, we remember the lives lost and the families whose lives were forever changed.
 
Western North Carolina has made great strides in recovery, thanks to the resilience of its people and those who have stood beside them. But much work remains.
 
I will continue fighting to ensure North Carolinians are not forgotten and that WNC receives the support it needs to be made whole again.
Happy birthday to my friend, Chairman @ChuckGrassley! It is an honor to serve alongside you. Wishing you a wonderful day.

Inflation is hurting working families across North Carolina and our nation. The Fed made the right decision yesterday to unanimously raise rates, and I thank Chairman Warsh for his leadership and displaying the independence needed to get prices under control for everyday Americans.

This is not the end for the Clarity Act. We've made substantial bipartisan progress in large part because of the White House. This procedural motion allows us to continue working towards a positive outcome. https://t.co/mNFxcGMtfU

Congratulations to @CissieGLynch on her nomination to serve as the U.S. Ambassador at Large for International Religious Freedom. President Trump made an excellent choice in selecting a North Carolinian who understands the importance of defending religious freedom at home and around the world.

President Trump is right: communism is an inhuman ideology that brings only death and destruction.
 
Vladimir Putin is the latest authoritarian carrying forward that brutal Soviet legacy, aligning with Iran and North Korea to undermine democracy. We have seen the savagery of that ambition firsthand in Ukraine.
 
"Win-win" strategies work in the private sector, but there is no middle ground between freedom and totalitarian aggression. We cannot accommodate a dictator bent on destroying sovereign democracies. American strength and resolve are the only answers.

In the aftermath of September 11th, our NATO Allies invoked Article 5 for the first time in history to answer the call to defend freedom. We will never forget the 2,459 American servicemembers and 1,100 coalition servicemembers, including 457 from the UK and 158 from Canada, who made the ultimate sacrifice serving in Afghanistan. America remains forever grateful to Allies for answering the call and for their sacrifice.

25 years ago, our nation was forever changed.

Today, we remember the nearly 3,000 lives lost on September 11, honor the heroes who answered the call and pray for the families who carry that loss.

We will never forget. 🇺🇸

As we approach the 25th anniversary of September 11th, I am reminded of the remarkable story of Operation Yellow Ribbon. When American airspace closed after the attacks, more than 6,500 stranded travelers were welcomed by the people of Gander, Newfoundland who housed and fed them until the crisis was over. In our darkest hour, our Canadian neighbors demonstrated extraordinary compassion.

Susan and I are praying for the brave CMPD officer shot in the line of duty this morning, their family and the entire CMPD community. We are grateful the officer is in stable condition and wish them a full and speedy recovery. https://t.co/F1Cwa2t3yy

I thank @SecArmy Dan Driscoll for his leadership to our Army and service to our country. Dan was the right man at the right moment to lead our Soldiers and Army civilians. 

Our understanding and assumptions of warfare are being challenged in places like Ukraine and Iran, and Dan understands the old way of doing business no longer applies. He and General George began a transformative period of innovation in how we array our forces and equip our Soldiers. He challenged our legacy approach to manning and procurement. Most of all, he cared deeply about the men and women in our Army formations and quickly earned their respect. 

If we had a @SecWar who maintained the same priorities and forward-thinking, he would be fighting to retain talented leaders like Dan and the many flag officers he has forced into retirement. Instead, he is creating a leadership void at the top of our military ranks. 

I served on Senate Armed Services for 8 years and as chair or ranking member of the Personnel and Readiness subcommittee. I have never witnessed more inept management of the brave men and women who serve our country. He is intimidated by competence and retreats to ginning up culture wars instead of soberly attending to the vital work of our national defense and the health and well-being of our fighting force. 

I urge the President to find a new leader at the Pentagon who will retain and empower our military talent rather than diminish it.

https://t.co/M58gSjtpCr

Big win for Beaufort and coastal North Carolina: NOAA’s historic Beaufort Laboratory is being rebuilt. I was proud to secure $64 million for the new facility, keeping world-class marine research in North Carolina for generations to come.
https://t.co/qTdZPKxkDs

America has lost a true national treasure. Dolly Parton’s extraordinary talent was matched only by her kindness, generosity and devotion to others. Susan and I are praying for the Parton family and all who loved her. May she rest in peace. https://t.co/ndqNbceJyA

Hosting the G20 Finance Ministerial in Asheville is a big win for Western North Carolina. It will bring global leaders, business executives and millions in economic activity to the region while showcasing how far our mountain communities have come in rebuilding after Helene.
https://t.co/bP6HGDZO5I

A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. financial_disclosures.note: Senate financial disclosures are filed through efd.senate.gov, a different system from the House Clerk index used here. Senate filings are not listed yet.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
